static_findings.snippet: - Don't use `eval()` or assign directly to `document.cookie`

- Avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` unless absolutely necessary
- Avoid spread syntax in accumulators within loops
- Avoid barrel files (index files that re-export everything)
- Avoid done callbacks in async tests — use async/await instead
- Keep test suites reasonably flat — avoid excessive `describe` nesting

content.value_statement: JavaScript and TypeScript projects need consistent linting, formatting, and upgrade practices. This skill guides Ultracite setup, configuration migration, code review, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Identify Ultracite installation and detect Oxlint, Biome, or ESLint configuration.
Guide initialization with package manager, framework, editor, agent, and integration options.
Select check, fix, and doctor commands for linting, formatting, and setup diagnostics.
Guide existing configuration migration and apply version-specific upgrade instructions.
Review JavaScript and TypeScript against documented type safety, accessibility, security, performance, and testing standards.
Explain framework presets, type-aware linting, and optional JavaScript plugins.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and references; actual linting requires installed external tools.
Linting cannot establish business logic correctness or replace tests and architectural review.
Preset coverage and type-aware support differ across linter backends and frameworks.
Initialization, fixes, upgrades, and hooks can change project files or install dependencies.

use_cases.title: Set Up a New Project
use_cases.description: Choose a linter backend and configure Ultracite presets for a TypeScript application.

use_cases.title: Migrate an Existing Repository
use_cases.description: Move existing lint configuration onto Ultracite while preserving custom rules and introducing stricter checks gradually.

use_cases.title: Standardize Code Review
use_cases.description: Review code for documented type safety, accessibility, async correctness, and testing practices alongside the repository formatter.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the Current Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project for Ultracite and identify its linter backend. Explain the appropriate read-only checks without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Ultracite
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Ultracite initialization for this React TypeScript project using its existing package manager. Ask before installing dependencies or changing editor, agent, or hook configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current lint and format configuration for migration to Ultracite. Preserve custom rules and propose staged changes with checks after each step.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Major Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our Ultracite configuration against the included upgrade guides, oldest first. Preserve custom rules and identify applicable preset, type-aware, and editor changes.

output_examples.input: What should I review beyond formatter output?
output: Check async error handling, input validation, semantic HTML, and accessible controls.
Review business logic, architecture, edge cases, and test assertions separately.

best_practices: Detect the installed Ultracite version, package manager, and linter backend before selecting commands or presets.
Review file changes after fixes or initialization, and preserve custom configuration unless a documented migration requires changes.
Apply upgrade guides in order and validate each stage with doctor, check, and relevant project tests.
anti_patterns: Using a download runner for routine checks when the repository already has a compatible installed version.
Leaving migration suppressions or disabled rules indefinitely without a plan to restore them.
Deleting active formatter configuration or enabling hooks and optional plugins without reviewing their effects.

faq.question: Which linter backends does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Oxlint with Oxfmt, Biome, and ESLint with Prettier and Stylelint.

faq.question: Does the skill include the Ultracite executable?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions and reference documents. Commands require the relevant packages and package manager.

faq.question: Can I keep my existing linter?
faq.answer: Yes. Migration can preserve the current backend while extending Ultracite presets and retaining custom rules.

faq.question: Does it enforce one formatting style?
faq.answer: No. The instructions defer to the repository's configured formatter settings.

faq.question: Is type-aware linting enabled for every project?
faq.answer: No. Support and configuration depend on the backend, installed dependencies, selected presets, and project choices.

faq.question: Can its workflows modify project files?
faq.answer: Yes. Fixes, initialization, upgrades, and optional hooks can write files. Initialization and upgrades can also install dependencies.
